lines.text: The Hounds came into the Lowmarket at dawn, with royal soldiers behind them and a list of every cellar in the district.
They got as far as the new fountain.
Someone had opened every tap on my aqueduct at once. The square was a lake. And standing in it, ankle-deep, were two thousand people who'd never had clean water before.
Clear the square! By order of the Grand Measurer!
This is our water, and our square. You want to search it, come and get your boots wet.
Nobody had asked them to. I would have told them not to. Which is probably why nobody asked me.
The first stone came from somewhere at the back. Then a bucket. Then a whole cart. And the Lowmarket rose.
While every Hound in the district fought a lake full of washerwomen, we walked to the river with coal sacks on our backs.
There's a coal barge at the Tanner's Steps. Its master owes me money. Well. He owes House Corrow money. He doesn't know I've left.
Oswin carried Nell in a coal basket. She told everyone afterwards it was the best day of her life.
We were halfway down the steps when the first blow landed. Not on me. On someone in the square.
A thread went sharp. Then another. Then a dozen at once, like hail on a roof.
I felt every one of them. A woman's arm, broken by a shield. A boy thrown against a wall. An old man, kicked, and kicked again.
Stop. We have to go back. They're being hurt because of me.
Go back, and every blow they took this morning was for nothing. Get on the barge, my lord. That's an order.
Oswin had never given me an order in his life. Then he picked me up and put me on the barge like a sack of coal.
The soldiers at the river gate had all run to the square to fight the washerwomen. Nobody searched one more barge of coal.
I lay under the coal, counting threads. By the time the walls were behind us, I had counted forty-one sharp ones.
Nell laid her hand on my chest, over the place the threads come from. She didn't say anything. It helped more than it should have.
That night, looking back from the river, we could see smoke over the Lowmarket. The Order was teaching it a lesson.
They'll remember this, Lucan. Not the lesson. The water.
At dawn, the barge came round a bend into Corrow waters. Across the river, from bank to bank, hung a great iron chain.
Ah. She's expecting us.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and twelve, coming soon.
